newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PALMER SAYS HIS CANCER HAS BEEN "CONTAINED".
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PALMER SAYS HIS CANCER HAS BEEN "CONTAINED".

text.p: Golf legend Arnold Palmer said Friday his doctors said his prostate cancer had been "contained."

Palmer, 67, underwent surgery earlier this month, and said "at the moment I'm faced with no treatment. I have the unpleasantness of wearing a catheter for a while. With a little luck, in a short period of time I will have my facilities back.

"I've just had the staples removed from surgery. I won't say there's not some discomfort and that I don't get a bit tired towards evening," said Palmer, who is credited with popularising the game in the television era.
Palmer, who ranks fourth on the all-time PGA Tour victory list with 60 titles said he was finding it difficult to follow doctor's orders and stay away from golf.

"Not doing really very much of anything for six weeks is something ... that I haven't faced in years," said Palmer, who won four Masters titles, two British Opens and one U.S. Open in his legendary career, which also includes 10 Senior titles.
"The last time I haven't swung a golf club in six weeks was about 1955. That is something that's going to be very difficult for me," Palmer told reporters at a news conference.
Palmer, 67, said he was feeling tired, but that his doctors said he was recovering well from the surgery.
"If something went wrong and I had to answer to the Lord, I was ready (but) I won't say I wasn't scared," Palmer said. "I was like anyone else would have been. I was very concerned."
Palmer said he opted for surgery to remove the cancer, rather than other forms of treatment, because he wanted to give them "every chance of getting it out".
He had "every intention" of playing the Masters at Augusta starting April 10 and he hoped to return for the Bay Hill Invitational, an event he hosts, starting March 20.
